# Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta (MN 10 (PTS MN i 55))
**ID:** MN 10 (PTS MN i 55)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Satipaṭṭhānasutta* (MN 10) is the tenth discourse in the *Majjhimanikāya*, addressed to the monks and setting out the four establishments of mindfulness as the direct path to Nibbāna and the seventh factor of the noble eightfold path [SuttaCentral; Shonin et al. 2015; Anālayo 2003]. The sutta organizes meditative practice into four sequential domains: contemplation of the body (*kāya*), feelings (*vedanā*), mind (*citta*), and mind-objects or phenomena (*dhamma*) [SuttaCentral; Anālayo 2014; Wen]. Within body contemplation, it incorporates the first tetrad of mindfulness of breathing, awareness of the four bodily postures, bodily anatomical parts, and charnel ground reflections [Anālayo 2014; Anālayo 2019; Wen].
SuttaCentral identifies full parallels in the *Dīghanikāya* (DN 22), the *Madhyama Āgama* (MĀ 98), the *Ekottarika Āgama* (EĀ 12.1), and a Sanskrit fragment (SHT sutta11), with shared sections also appearing in the *Kāyagatāsati Sutta* (MN 119; MĀ 81) and *Saccavibhaṅga Sutta* (MN 141) [SuttaCentral; Anālayo 2014; Anālayo 2019]. DharmaNexus strongly corroborates these relationships, identifying over 233,000 shared characters with DN 22 (§0.2–44.3) and substantial Pali-internal reuse with the *Satipaṭṭhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 7), SN 47, and MN 119, while aligning passages cross-linguistically with the Chinese Āgamas and Sanskrit and Tibetan treatises including the *Śikṣāsamuccaya*, *Śrāvakabhūmi*, and *Prajñāpāramitā* texts [DharmaNexus]. Accompanied by its commentary, MN 10 has served as a foundational source for Theravāda meditation manuals and remains central to the 20th-century *vipassanā* revival and contemporary mindfulness practice [Crosby; Stanley et al. 2018; Walshe 1987].
